points.horizonLabel: Latest GDP, GDPNow and core PCE
points.title: Published growth and core-inflation anchors
points.summary: Growth is 1.45pp above the assumed 2.0% trend, using Real GDP growth 3.4% and Atlanta Fed GDPNow 3.5%. Core PCE is 3.1% y/y, 1.10pp above the 2% target. GDP and GDPNow cover different quarters. Ranges are sensitivity assumptions (±0.6pp growth, ±0.25pp inflation), not empirically calibrated confidence intervals.

evidence.interpretation: Real GDP growth: 3.4% (Q3 2026 quarter-on-quarter annualized GDP); Atlanta Fed GDPNow: 3.5% (Fourth-Quarter GDPNow Estimate for 2026:Q4 (nowcast; not an official forecast))
BEA core PCE: 3.1% year over year (2026-09); target: 2.0%.

points.title: Weekly market commentary | BlackRock Investment Institute
points.summary: BlackRock emphasizes AI investment support and persistent inflation alongside funding and slowdown risks. The 2.3% growth and 3.1% core-inflation equivalents are our qualitative mapping, not BlackRock numerical forecasts. Both axes have broad uncertainty.

evidence.quote: investment supports economic growth and risk assets
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.30%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

evidence.quote: We see inflation settling above pre-pandemic levels
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 3.10%; target 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

points.title: Weekly Trader's Outlook
points.summary: Schwab describes firm growth, sticky inflation and a stable labor market. We map that qualitative current backdrop to 2.6% real growth and a 3.0% core-inflation equivalent. Both are our inferred numerical translation, not Schwab-published forecasts, and their uncertainty ranges are deliberately broad.

evidence.quote: Growth remains relatively firm
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.60%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

evidence.quote: inflationary pressures appear somewhat sticky
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 3.00%; target 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

points.title: Monthly Market Review
points.summary: The review highlights strong U.S. activity, elevated inflation and a restrictive financing backdrop. We map that backdrop to above-trend growth and above-target inflation. The 2.5% growth and 3.0% core-inflation proxies are inferred from the commentary, not published J.P. Morgan forecasts; the quoted Fed assessment is supporting context.

evidence.quote: upgraded economic activity from ‘solid’ to ‘strong
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.50%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

evidence.quote: while describing inflation as ‘elevated
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 3.00%; target 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

outlookDirection.horizonLabel: Next 6–12 months; global baseline applied to the U.S.

evidence.quote: inflation moderates as the energy price shock fades
evidence.interpretation: PIMCO’s global cyclical baseline expects moderating inflation. Applying that direction to this U.S. map is our interpretation; no U.S.-specific numerical destination is stated.

points.title: Growth Holds, Risks Widen
points.summary: PIMCO’s baseline is resilient growth with moderating inflation, while geopolitical and AI risks widen the possible outcomes. Applying its global cyclical argument to the U.S., we infer 2.4% growth and a 2.6% core-inflation equivalent. Cooling inflation remains above the 2% target; these mapped numbers are not published PIMCO forecasts.

evidence.quote: stable global growth to continue in our baseline
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.40%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

evidence.quote: inflation moderates as the energy price shock fades
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 2.60%; target 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

outlookDirection.horizonLabel: Forward outlook; end date not specified by Waldron

evidence.quote: We obviously think as a firm inflation will start to migrate down
evidence.interpretation: John Waldron expects inflation to move down. The excerpt gives no dated inflation endpoint or growth-rate change; this is his commentary, not a formal probability forecast.

points.title: John Waldron on GDP Growth, AI, and the M&A Outlook
points.summary: Waldron explicitly describes an approximately 2.5% real-growth forecast and expects inflation to move down. The 2.8% core-inflation equivalent is our interpretation of that qualitative outlook, not a numerical Goldman inflation forecast. The point remains above trend and target even as inflation cools.

evidence.quote: 2.5% real growth plus minus
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.50%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: direct.

evidence.quote: inflation will start to migrate down
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 2.80%; target 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

evidence.quote: Inflation remains above target but should ease as energy costs fall and rents cool
evidence.interpretation: ING expects inflation to ease while above target. The point’s numerical core-inflation equivalent is our mapping, not a published endpoint.

points.title: Solid growth and cooling inflation: 3 calls for the US
points.summary: ING gives a 2–2.5% growth baseline; the plotted growth rate is its midpoint. Its base case expects inflation to ease with energy, rents and wages. We infer a 2.7% core-inflation equivalent with a broad range. The plotted scenario is its baseline, excluding the separate Iran-risk and AI-boom scenarios.

evidence.quote: respectable US growth of 2-2.5
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.25%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: direct.

evidence.quote: Inflation remains above target but should ease
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 2.70%; target 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

outlookDirection.horizonLabel: By April 2027; later than the plotted year-end 2026 forecast

evidence.quote: By April 2027, that mechanical effect alone should bring core inflation as measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index toward 2.5%, a meaningful decline from current levels
evidence.interpretation: Vanguard describes a decline toward 2.5% core PCE by April 2027. Its plotted endpoint is 3.2% for year-end 2026; this later directional statement does not determine that endpoint’s arrow.

points.title: Our economic outlook for the United States
points.summary: Vanguard explicitly raises its year-end core-inflation forecast to 3.2%, while expecting tariff-related disinflation in 2027. We infer 2.3% growth from its balanced-economy discussion with a wide growth range; that growth number is not a Vanguard forecast. The inflation coordinate uses the year-end forecast, not its lower April 2027 expectation.

evidence.quote: while preserving labor-market balance
evidence.interpretation: Mapped real growth 2.30%; trend benchmark 2.0%. Basis: inferred.

evidence.quote: 2026 core inflation forecast to 3.2
evidence.interpretation: Mapped core-inflation equivalent 3.20%; target 2.0%. Basis: direct.

points.title: How will Fed rate hikes impact markets?
points.summary: Current growth is inferred from the CIO’s discussion of recent GDP and firm activity. The inflation discussion cites CPI, not core PCE: 2.9% is our approximate core-PCE-equivalent, not a UBS forecast.

evidence.quote: US GDP growth was close to 2.5% annualized in the first half of the year and tracked near 3% in the third quarter.
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.75% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

evidence.quote: High energy prices and strong US economic data have added to inflation concerns.
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 2.9%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

points.title: Rate-of-Change Season: Digesting Peak Growth in a Volatile Stretch
points.summary: Citi Wealth CIO expects continued but slower capex growth and building inflation pressure. Both coordinates are our approximate mapping of that argument. Strong nominal growth and company earnings are not treated as published real-GDP forecasts.

evidence.quote: Hyperscaler capex and issuance should keep rising for years but expected spending growth has slowed.
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.3% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±1pp.

evidence.quote: We expect the Fed to stay behind the curve, which supports strong nominal growth but raises the risk of higher inflation for the medium-term.
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 3.2%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.9pp.

points.institution: Bank of America Private Bank CIO
points.title: BofA CIO economic research
points.summary: The Private Bank CIO sees continued expansion with benign wage pressures and strong productivity. The coordinates are our qualitative mapping. The report’s separate BofA Global Research table uses core CPI, so it is not represented as a direct core-PCE forecast.

evidence.quote: setting the stage for continued economic expansion and an ongoing but more tempered bull market in Equities in 2027.
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.3% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.9pp.

evidence.quote: With wage pressures benign, productivity strong and the early-cycle acceleration set to peak, we believe the odds of an aggressive tightening cycle that derails the bull market are low.
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 2.7%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

points.title: Wells Fargo economic research
points.summary: WFII expects supportive economic growth in 2027 and flags diesel pass-through into core prices. Both rates are our estimates; the inflation discussion is near term and does not supply a matched 2027 core-PCE forecast. The comparison path is interpretive.

evidence.quote: We expect economic growth and corporate earnings to remain supportive in 2027
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.5% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.9pp.

evidence.quote: Diesel prices have outpaced gasoline and crude oil, raising the cost of moving goods and adding pressure to core inflation
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 3.1%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.9pp.

points.title: Weekly Bottom Line
points.summary: TD’s current assessment emphasizes resilient labor conditions and broad price pressure. Both numeric levels are our interpretation of current commentary, not published forecasts; CPI evidence is translated approximately into core-PCE-equivalent units.

evidence.quote: This combination of labor market resilience and persistent price pressures gives the Fed room to remain focused on inflation.
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.5% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

evidence.quote: inflationary pressures appeared fairly broad-based across categories in the October report, and showed little sign of cooling.
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 3.2%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.7pp.

points.horizonLabel: Q4 2026; GDP Q4/Q4, core PCE y/y
points.title: Monthly Economic Outlook | U.S. Bank
points.summary: Both endpoint rates are explicit U.S. Bank forecasts for Q4 2026. Its separate 2027 forecasts are slower growth and lower inflation. The issue states November 2026; no publication day is claimed. Ellipse widths remain our sensitivity assumptions.

evidence.quote: Real GDP growth is forecast at 2.5% Q4-over-Q4 in 2026 (2.4% annual average) and 2.0% in 2027 (2.2% annual average).
evidence.interpretation: Published forecast / range midpoint: 2.5% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.4pp.

evidence.quote: We expect core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation to average 3.2% year-over-year in Q4 2026 before moderating to 2.5% by the end of 2027
evidence.interpretation: Published core PCE forecast: 3.2%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.35pp.

points.title: Global Outlook - US:The energy shock fades, the AI boom doesn’t
points.summary: ABN AMRO explicitly forecasts core PCE around 2.4% at end-2027. The 2.3% growth coordinate is our inference from investment-supported expansion, not its published numerical GDP forecast. Current Q3 GDP is not substituted for the forward endpoint.

evidence.quote: Investment will keep driving growth in 2027, consumers keep up as falling inflation lifts real incomes.
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.3% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

evidence.quote: Our forecast is for core PCE inflation to ease only gradually, from 3.1% now to around 2.4% by the end of 2027.
evidence.interpretation: Published core PCE forecast: 2.4%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.5pp.

points.title: HSBC AM Investment Monthly - Profits power ahead
points.summary: HSBC AM describes robust but uneven U.S. demand and increased supply-side risks. Both coordinates are approximate interpretations of current conditions. The risk tilt is not converted into a quantified stagflation base case or a forecast path.

evidence.quote: US domestic demand is robust but uneven
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 2.25% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±1pp.

evidence.quote: Upside inflation risks and downside growth risks have increased accordingly
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 3%; target 2%. Model half-width ±1pp.

points.title: Rochdale Speedometers: November 2026
points.summary: The growth coordinate is the midpoint of RBC Rochdale’s explicit 2–2.5% forecast. Its inflation measure is not specified as core PCE; the 3% core-PCE-equivalent coordinate is inferred with a wider range. This is RBC Rochdale, not RBC Capital Markets.

evidence.quote: economic growth of 2% to 2.5% in both 2026 and 2027.
evidence.interpretation: Published forecast / range midpoint: 2.25% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.5pp.

evidence.quote: We have raised our year-end 2026 inflation forecast to a range of 2.75% to 3.25%
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 3%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

points.title: UBP House View - November 2026
points.summary: Growth is the midpoint of UBP’s published U.S. 2–2.5% range; core PCE is explicitly expected near 3%. The separate headline inflation forecast above 4% is not plotted as core inflation. Periods differ and the ellipse widths are ours.

evidence.quote: US growth is expected to remain within a range of 2.0 – 2.5% in 2026 – 2027.
evidence.interpretation: Published forecast / range midpoint: 2.25% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.5pp.

evidence.quote: core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation should remain close to 3%
evidence.interpretation: Published core PCE forecast: 3%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.5pp.

points.horizonLabel: Current conditions; Q3 GDP / October prices
points.title: BNP Paribas economic research
points.summary: BNP Paribas describes strong current activity and broad inflation pressure. The 3.2% growth and core-PCE-equivalent coordinates are our approximate current-condition mapping. Observed Q3 GDP of 3.4% is not presented as a future forecast; monthly CPI is not an annual core-PCE rate.

evidence.quote: The US macroeconomic performance has seemingly been unaffected by the energy shock
evidence.interpretation: Our qualitative mapping: 3.2% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

evidence.quote: October data were a reminder that the US inflation problem reaches beyond the rise in energy prices
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 3.2%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.8pp.

points.title: PNC economic research
points.summary: The report’s annual table has columns 2025, 2026f and 2027f. Its explicit 2027 endpoints are real GDP 2.2% and core PCE 2.5%, both Q4/Q4. The near-term statement that core PCE stays near 3% through Q1 2027 is a different horizon. October issue; exact publication day unavailable.

evidence.interpretation: Published forecast / range midpoint: 2.2% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.6pp.
Published core PCE forecast: 2.5%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.5pp.

points.title: Scotiabank economic research
points.summary: Scotiabank explicitly describes U.S. growth around 2.1% over the next two years. The 2.7% core-PCE-equivalent is our broad inference from persistent U.S. inflation and later normalization. Its total-PCE/CPI forecasts are not labeled direct core PCE. This PDF is dated October 13, not the newer index date.

evidence.quote: The broad U.S. growth outlook for 2026–28 is little changed, with growth close to potential and around 2.1% for the next two years.
evidence.interpretation: Published forecast / range midpoint: 2.1% real growth; assumed trend 2%. Model half-width ±0.6pp.

evidence.quote: Inflation pressures are proving more persistent in both Canada and the U.S.
evidence.interpretation: Our inferred core-PCE-equivalent: 2.7%; target 2%. Model half-width ±0.9pp.

indicators.name: Real GDP growth

indicators.name: Core PCE inflation

indicators.name: Atlanta Fed GDPNow
